rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about or consider an applicant's criminal record until after a conditional offer. They may never consider non-conviction, expunged, sealed, pardoned, vacated or juvenile records. After an offer, they may consider only listed serious convictions within set look-back periods, and a withdrawal needs an individualized assessment and written notice.
rules.key_value: Post-offer look-back: 6 years for first-degree, 4 years for second/third-degree, 1 year for fourth-degree indictable offenses
rules.penalty: Civil penalty up to $1,000 for a first violation, $5,000 for a second within five years, and $10,000 for two or more others within seven years; the director may also order the application fee returned and up to $1,000 paid to the applicant.
rules.status_basis: Takes effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment (approved June 18, 2021).

requires.name: rental_dwelling_unit
requires.text: a dwelling unit offered for rent by a housing provider for residential purposes

exempt_if.text: of not more than four dwelling units

coverage.summary: Applies to housing providers renting dwelling units to applicants.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded.

rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
